summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and prostate cancer undergoing radiation therapy was admitted for acute urinary retention and suspected UTI. He had a similar episode three weeks prior complicated by ESBL Klebsiella infection. On admission, he had suprapubic discomfort, elevated creatinine, and a positive urinalysis. Urine culture confirmed ESBL Klebsiella, and he was treated with ciprofloxacin. He developed C. difficile colitis, likely antibiotic-related, and was started on oral vancomycin. His acute kidney injury, attributed to dehydration, improved with cautious IV hydration. Tacrolimus levels were subtherapeutic and dose was increased. Doxazosin was initiated for urinary retention, and carvedilol was reduced due to overlapping hypotensive effects. He completed scheduled radiation therapy during admission. By discharge, his infection was resolving, renal function had normalized, and he was stable on adjusted medications with follow-up plans.
